note: CATCH-UP RUN: Thursday 10 Sep 2026, ~18:10-18:55 SGT (an evening run, not the usual pre-Asia-open slot), covering the full gap since the 4 Sep run -- Fri 5 Sep through today. NY is currently Thu pre-market; the latest completed US session is Wed 9 Sep. At least 4 items below are dated 9-10 Sep specifically (PPI/CPI pending, Hormuz escalation, MP Materials conference, BTC/CLARITY status); the rest sweep the full week for the highest-decision-relevance items given the multi-day gap.

items.headline: August payrolls blow past estimates at +162K, reviving Fed hike fears
items.summary: August Non-Farm Payrolls printed +162,000 versus a 55,000 consensus (unemployment held at 4.1%), a sharp beat that immediately revived odds of a HIKE (not a cut) at the Sep 15-16 FOMC. The Dow fell 271pts (-0.51%) and the 2-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since Jan 2025 on the print.
items.actionable: Flips the macro setup from the 3 Sep Waller-driven dovish rally back toward genuine two-sided risk into the FOMC -- the levered silver/miners book now faces a real rate headwind alongside its Hormuz-driven haven tailwind.

items.headline: New Fed Chair Warsh stays hawkish, Governor Waller the lone dovish dissenter, into a genuine coin-flip FOMC
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has held a hawkish line since his Jackson Hole remarks ('we have work to do'), while Governor Waller argues underlying disinflation trends are better than headline data suggests. CME-style odds have run 48-60% for a 25bp hike at the Sep 15-16 meeting through the week -- a genuinely live, two-sided outcome pending today's PPI and tomorrow's CPI.
items.actionable: A real hike-vs-hold coin-flip is now priced for the FOMC -- the large cash pile is well-positioned to redeploy either way, but a hike would pressure the levered silver and SGX REIT sides of the book simultaneously.

items.headline: PPI today, CPI tomorrow are the decisive prints before the Sep 15-16 FOMC
items.summary: August PPI is due today (10 Sep, 8:30am ET) and August CPI tomorrow (11 Sep), with headline CPI consensus around 3.4% y/y. Both prints are seen as decisive for whether Chair Warsh's hawkish camp or Governor Waller's dovish camp prevails at next week's FOMC meeting.
items.actionable: The single biggest near-term catalyst for the whole book -- a hot print would raise hike odds and pressure REITs/miners' rate-sensitive gains simultaneously; a cool print would validate the doves and could extend the precious-metals bid.

items.headline: Hormuz conflict escalates further -- IRGC claims strikes on vessels including US ships, Brent tops $100
items.summary: The IRGC claimed new strikes on vessels it accused of violating its restricted zone, including two US-linked ships. Brent settled near $97.89 on 9/8 and traded through $100.29 early on 9/9 -- its first time above $100 in six weeks. Iran separately rejected a US-proposed transit-fee framework and said it is 'ready for a more intense conflict'; Houthi forces struck Saudi energy infrastructure, widening the disruption regionally. Eurasia Group now pushes any real de-escalation to year-end.
items.actionable: This is a genuinely longer, structurally worsening conflict, not a fading headline risk -- supportive of maintaining precious-metals exposure and the cash pile as hedges, and a real cost headwind via energy prices for the broader portfolio.

items.headline: Gold miners fully reverse Barrick's 2 Sep IPO-delay slump; one of the sector's best weeks in years
items.summary: After falling roughly 5% on 2 Sep on a Bloomberg report of a possible IPO delay, Barrick rallied back through the week alongside a broad gold-miner surge tied to elevated bullion prices and renewed Hormuz-driven haven demand; the Aug 10 Newmont settlement ($1.95bn, resolving the Nevada JV dispute) remains a supportive background factor. Silver has held a $66-68/oz range this week, up roughly 63% y/y. No new Barrick-specific catalyst emerged -- this looks like sector beta reasserting itself after an overreaction.
items.actionable: Confirms the 2 Sep Barrick dip was idiosyncratic governance/timing noise rather than a read-through on the broader miners thesis -- the levered silver/gold-miners sleeve remains intact and has fully round-tripped the drawdown.

items.headline: Reuters: Chinese rare-earth suppliers quietly refusing shipments to US customers since early August
items.summary: Some Chinese rare-earth suppliers have declined to ship to US customers since early August -- even holding valid export licenses -- reportedly fearing Beijing retaliation after China sanctioned a supply-chain auditor (the Responsible Business Alliance). Prices of yttrium, indium phosphide and tungsten remain near record highs on tight supply. MP Materials and USA Rare Earth were both named as directly exposed, with the issue now on the agenda ahead of Xi Jinping's planned 24 Sep Washington visit.
items.actionable: Direct, dated confirmation of the core ex-China rare-earth watchlist thesis -- China is using informal/gray-zone leverage even where formal export controls are suspended, reinforcing the case for MP/Lynas/Energy Fuels exposure into the Sep 24 Xi visit as a binary catalyst.

items.headline: China August exports jump 25% y/y; semiconductor exports surge 130%
items.summary: China's customs data showed August exports up 25% y/y (autos +43%, semiconductor exports +129.8%), with the trade surplus widening to $119.1bn from $112.5bn. Exports to the US rose 34.4% despite ongoing trade tensions.
items.actionable: Resilient Chinese trade/tech-export data is a modest positive read-through for the HK tech basket broadly, though it did not prevent this week's shared macro-driven (Fed/oil/yields) selloff across Tencent, SMIC and Xiaomi.

items.headline: Xiaomi keeps sliding despite Sept 7 foldable/EV launch blitz; EV delivery target badly missed
items.summary: Xiaomi's 7 Sep autumn event (Xiaomi 18 Fold, Pad 9 Pro Max, three 'Sky Nomad' EVs) failed to arrest the stock's decline -- shares fell to roughly HK$25.92 by 10 Sep, down 8.9% on the week and about 54% below the 52-week high. Cumulative EV deliveries through August reached only 246,322 units, just 44.8% of the 550,000 full-year target, while smartphone shipments fell 26% y/y last quarter and revenue fell 11% y/y, its first decline in roughly three years.
items.actionable: The week's ~9% Xiaomi decline is fundamentally driven by execution concerns (EV delivery shortfall, margin pressure), not a single headline -- the product launch failed to offset those worries, a genuine negative mark for the HK tech leg of the book distinct from Tencent/SMIC's shared macro-driven weakness.

items.headline: STI hits fresh intraday record (5,807) on bank/property strength, before giving it back through the week
items.summary: The Straits Times Index rose roughly 1% to an intraday record 5,807.16 on 4 Sep, led by DBS, OCBC and UOB (each +0.7-1.2%) as broader Asian equities rallied on easing US Treasury yields. The index has since pulled back to 5,689.75 by 10 Sep (-1.9%) as the hawkish NFP surprise reversed the rate-cut optimism that drove the record.
items.actionable: Confirms Singapore banks remain a genuine rate-cycle beneficiary on the way up, but the subsequent hawkish NFP-driven reversal is the key risk to watch for whether the record high holds or the pullback extends into the FOMC.

items.headline: S-REITs lag badly YTD as renewed rate-hike odds reintroduce duration risk
items.summary: The FTSE ST All-Share REIT Index is down 8.2% YTD (as of 4 Sep) versus the FTSE STI's +24.6% gain, despite REIT managers delivering resilient distribution growth this earnings season. The narrative has flipped from expected Fed cuts earlier in 2026 to now-live hike odds, pressuring yield-sensitive REIT valuations even though underlying property fundamentals have not deteriorated.
items.actionable: The S-REIT book faces a genuine headwind if the Sep 15-16 FOMC delivers a hike -- distributions remain sound, but rate-driven multiple compression is the dominant near-term risk, distinct from the (more resilient) SGX bank exposure.

items.headline: MP Materials reiterates DoD-backed buildout at Jefferies conference amid a structurally tight rare-earth market
items.summary: MP Materials CFO Ryan Corbett presented at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference on 9 Sep, reiterating progress on the DoD-backed '10X' magnet facility (production targeted end-2028) and the Saudi Ma'aden/DoD refining joint venture, while acknowledging continued pressure from Chinese export restrictions and a structurally tight NdPr market.
items.actionable: Reinforces the long-term DoD-backing thesis for MP but confirms near-term execution timelines (2028) remain distant -- the watchlist thesis is intact rather than accelerating this week.

items.headline: Bitcoin drifts to ~$78K as the Sep 15 CLARITY Act vote approaches with sharply fading odds
items.summary: Bitcoin trades near $77,970-79,500, down roughly 4% on the week from ~$81K on 3 Sep, with a bearish MACD crossover signaling fading momentum. The critical CLARITY Act Senate cloture vote is set for 15 Sep -- the same day as the FOMC decision. Polymarket-style pricing on 2026 passage has fallen to roughly 10-25% across trackers (from an 82% February peak), with sticking points on stablecoin-rewards language and Trump-family crypto ethics provisions; seven Democratic senators have made support conditional on text changes.
items.actionable: Deteriorating legislative odds into a vote stacked on FOMC day create a plausible negative catalyst overlap for crypto-adjacent risk sentiment -- notably, crypto-specific Fear&Greed has stayed in Greed (69) even as equity sentiment fell to Fear (36), a divergence worth treating with caution rather than as a buy signal.
